Katalon Studio: Install & Setup.sum: Activate your license, install Katalon Studio, log in and start the Practitioner course.
Katalon Studio: Install & Setup.intro: This lesson gets you ready to practise with Katalon. You will activate your license, install and open Katalon Studio, log in, and start the Practitioner Level Certification course on Katalon Academy. Follow the steps in order. Every step has a screenshot so you can check you are in the right place.
need: The invitation email for your Katalon license
A computer where you can install apps
An internet connection

parts.s: Your admin invites you by email. Accepting the invitation turns on your license.

steps.d: Open your inbox and look for an email called “Invitation to Join My Account_01 on Katalon” from the Katalon Team.
steps.tip: Can’t see it? Check your Spam or Promotions folder. Still missing? Ask your KT admin to send it again.
steps.cap: The Katalon invitation email

steps.d: Press the green Accept invitation button inside the email. This activates your license.

steps.t: Sign up or log in to Katalon
steps.d: A Katalon page opens. Choose how you want to sign in: Google, GitHub, SSO or email. If you do not have a Katalon account yet, click Sign up and create one.
steps.tip: Use the same email address that received the invitation.
steps.cap: The Katalon log in page

steps.d: Select the first option, My Account_01, then click Continue.
steps.note: You may see two accounts with the same name. Choose the first one in the list.
steps.cap: Choose the domain you wish to access

parts.t: Install Katalon Studio and log in
parts.s: Katalon Studio is the app you will use for every activity in this course.

steps.d: If Katalon Studio is not on your computer yet, download it with the button below and install it.
steps.note: Already installed? Skip to the next step.

steps.d: Search for Katalon Studio on your computer and open it.

steps.t: Log in with your license account
steps.d: On the Welcome screen, click Log in from Browser and sign in with the account you just activated.
steps.note: You can log in from the browser or through the License server. Use the one your admin tells you to use.
steps.cap: Welcome to Katalon Studio

steps.t: Check that you are logged in
steps.d: Click the account icon at the top right of Katalon Studio. The menu shows which account you are logged in with. If you see your account there, you are ready.
steps.cap: The account menu in Katalon Studio

parts.s: Katalon Academy gives you free courses and tracks your progress toward the certificate.

steps.d: Go to your Katalon Academy profile and open Certifications.
Find L1 – Practitioner Level Certification and click Learn more to unlock it.
steps.cap: Practitioner Level Certification, before it is unlocked

steps.d: Once it is unlocked, find the note that says “we recommend enrolling in these courses” and click these courses.
steps.cap: The “these courses” link

steps.d: You will land on a course page. Click Start Course to begin.
steps.note: The courses show you how to use Katalon. If you already know Katalon, you only need to finish the activities required for the Practitioner certificate.
steps.cap: A Katalon Academy course page

parts.t: Track your progress and get your certificate
parts.s: Do the activities, check your progress, and collect your certificate.

steps.t: Do your activities and check progress daily
steps.d: Work on the activities in Katalon Studio. Then check your Academy certification profile every day to see your percentage go up.
steps.warn: Your progress can take 1 to 2 days to update on Katalon Academy, so do not worry if it does not change right away.

steps.d: When your progress reaches 100%, you receive your Practitioner certificate. Katalon also sends it to your email.
steps.tip: Save it in this portal: go to Certifications → Practitioner and upload an image or PDF of your certificate.
steps.cap: The Practitioner Level Certification

Check your spam or promotions folder first. If it is not there, ask your KT admin to send the invitation again.

Recording a Manual Test as Automated.sum: Record your clicks once, then let Katalon replay them for you. No coding needed.
Recording a Manual Test as Automated.intro: Think of Record & Playback like a camcorder for your testing. You do a manual test once while Katalon watches and records every click and keystroke. Then Katalon replays it on demand, as many times as you like. In this lesson you will turn a simple manual test into your first automated one.
obj: Explain what Record & Playback does
Create a basic Web UI test case from a manual scenario
Record clicks and text entry
Save the captured page elements in the Object Repository
Run the test and check whether it passed or failed
need: Katalon Studio installed and activated, and able to open a project. Not yet? See Lesson 1: Install & Setup
A web browser such as Google Chrome
The CURA demo website: https://katalon-demo-cura.herokuapp.com/
About 45–60 minutes. Read the practice scenario below before you start.

info.d: It is the easiest way to create an automated test. You perform your manual test on a real website. Katalon Studio watches and turns each action into an automated step. Later, Playback repeats those steps by itself. You do not have to write any Groovy code.
info.cap: The five stages of Record & Playback: Prepare, Record, Perform, Save and Playback
info.tip: Each stage is one part of this lesson. The numbered steps below walk you through all five.

info.t: What does Katalon save for you?
info.d: When you stop recording, Katalon keeps two things. The test steps (what to do) go into your test case. The page elements (which button or box to click) go into the Object Repository. Think of the steps as a recipe and the Object Repository as the ingredients shelf.
info.cap: Test steps on one side, the page elements they use on the other. Your own recording will be shorter, because our test stops at the login page.

scn.t: Test case TC_WEB_001: Verify Login Page Navigation
scn.note: This test stops at the login page on purpose. You will not enter any username, password or data, so nothing can be changed on the site.

parts.s: You will do the test by hand while Katalon records every move. Take your time.

steps.d: Start Katalon Studio and open your project. Don't have one yet? Click File ▸ New ▸ Project, name it Test_Project, choose Web as the type, then click OK.
steps.cap: The New Project window: name it Test_Project and pick Web. (The Location field is hidden here for privacy. Yours will show a folder on your computer.)

steps.d: On the toolbar, click the Record Web button. It opens the Recorder window.
steps.cap: The Record Web button opens the Recorder window

steps.d:
In the Recorder window, do these three things:
1. Pick New Browser and choose a supported browser.
2. In the address box, type the CURA address: https://katalon-demo-cura.herokuapp.com/
3. If you see a selection mode, choose Basic.
steps.tip: The screenshot shows a different website address as an example. Type the CURA address instead.
steps.cap: The Recorder settings. Replace the example address with the CURA website.

steps.d: Click Start Record and wait. A browser window opens and loads the website. Do not click anything until the page has fully loaded.
Click Make Appointment on the CURA home page. Wait for the login page to appear. Stop there. Don't click anything else.
steps.tip: Katalon may record a few extra steps, such as a wait or a window setting. That is normal. Just keep the steps that match your scenario.
steps.cap: The CURA home page with the Make Appointment button

steps.d: A test needs to check something, otherwise it only clicks around. Right-click the Login heading on the page. Then choose Katalon Recorder Plus ▸ Assert Element State ▸ Present.
steps.note: Can't find that menu? No problem. You can add the same check later in Manual view by using the Verify Element Present keyword.
steps.cap: Right-click the Login heading and choose Assert Element State ▸ Present

steps.d: Close the recorder window by clicking Stop, then Save. Katalon shows you the recorded steps. Read through them: each line is one thing you did on the website.
steps.cap: The recorded steps. Yours may have a few more or fewer lines.

steps.d: Katalon asks where to keep the captured page elements. Choose a folder in the Object Repository. To make a new one, click New Folder and give it a clear name.
steps.cap: Choosing (or creating) an Object Repository folder

steps.d:
Give the test case a name that says what it does. Use exactly this one:
TC_WEB_001_Verify_Login_Page_Navigation
Then click OK. Your first automated test case is ready!
steps.tip: Good names save time later. Anyone should know what a test does just by reading its name.

parts.s: Now the fun part: let Katalon do all the clicking for you.

steps.d: In Test Explorer on the left, open Test Cases. Double-click TC_WEB_001_Verify_Login_Page_Navigation.

steps.t: Pick a browser to run on
steps.d: On the toolbar, open the Run drop-down arrow and choose a browser, for example Chrome.
steps.cap: Choosing a browser from the Run drop-down. This screenshot comes from another example project, so your test case name will be different.

steps.d: Click the green Run button and watch. The browser opens and repeats your clicks all by itself.
steps.tip: Don't touch the mouse or keyboard while the test runs. Just watch and enjoy!

steps.d: When the run ends, open the Log Viewer at the bottom. A green Passed means every step worked. A red Failed means something did not work. Click the failed line to see why.
steps.cap: The Log Viewer after a run. This example shows Passed. It comes from another project, so the step names differ.

concepts: One automated test. It is a list of steps.
The tool that watches you and records your actions.
One element on a page, such as a button or text box.
The folder where Katalon stores all the Test Objects.
Running the recorded test again, automatically.
A check that proves something is true, like "the heading is visible".
help: Recording does not start
Some versions of Katalon Studio (8.x and 9.x) have a known problem with Chrome 142. Try another supported browser, or use Active Browser mode instead of New Browser.
A click was not captured
No worries. Record the test again, and wait for each page to load before you click.
The test fails during playback
Open the Log Viewer and read the error. Then check that the page finished loading, that you chose the right browser, and that the Test Object still matches the page.
The test passes but checks nothing
A test with no verification only clicks around. Add a check, like the Login heading assertion in Step 6.
The object names are hard to understand
Names like Page_Login/button_Login are normal. Katalon builds them from the page and the element. Keep them or rename them clearly.

I recorded the three steps of the scenario
I added a verification (check) on the Login heading
I saved the page elements in the Object Repository
I named the test case TC_WEB_001_Verify_Login_Page_Navigation
I ran the test and read the result in the Log Viewer
done: I can explain Record & Playback in my own words
I created a Web UI test case from a manual scenario
My test case has a verification step
I can run it and tell if it passed or failed
I can name the parts that Katalon saved: test steps and Test Objects
res: Create test cases with Record & Playback

Recording a Manual Test as Automated.cert: Every test case and Test Object you record counts toward the Practitioner Certification goals (such as creating 50 test cases and 30 test objects). Keep recording!

Running Tests Locally & Reading Reports.sum: Run one test or a whole Test Suite on your own computer, then read the results and reports.
Running Tests Locally & Reading Reports.intro: You have recorded a test. Now let's run it! In this lesson you will run a single test case, run several tests together in a Test Suite, and learn how to read the results. Reading the report is how you find out whether your application is working.
obj: Run an automated test case on your computer
Run several test cases together in a Test Suite
Watch the execution and understand what is happening
Read the results in the Log Viewer
Find and understand the generated test report
need: Katalon Studio open with your training project
The test case you saved in Lesson 2. Need it? See Lesson 2: Record & Playback
The browser you will use (for example Google Chrome) installed on your computer

info.d: It means the test runs on your own computer. Katalon opens a real browser, repeats the steps you recorded, and saves the results on your computer. Later lessons will show how to run tests in the cloud with TestOps.

info.t: What do the result statuses mean?
info.d:
After every run, each test gets one of these statuses:
Passed The steps and checks all worked.
Failed A step or check did not match what was expected.
Error Something stopped the run, like a browser problem or a missing Test Object.
Skipped / Incomplete The test was not run, or did not finish.
info.tip: A test can pass even if it only clicks buttons. Always include a verification step to check the expected result.

parts.s: Start with the simplest run: one test, one browser.

steps.d: In Tests Explorer on the left, expand Test Cases. Double-click the test case you saved in Lesson 2.
On the toolbar, click the small drop-down arrow beside the Run button. Select Chrome (or another supported browser).
Click Run. Katalon opens the browser and repeats your recorded actions.
Let the test finish by itself.
steps.warn: Do not click or type in the browser that Katalon opened. Doing so can make your test fail.

parts.t: Run many tests in a Test Suite
parts.s: A Test Suite is a folder of test cases that run one after another. It is perfect for running many tests at once.

steps.d: In Tests Explorer, expand Test Suites and open an existing suite. If you don't have one, create it: right-click Test Suites, then choose New ▸ Test Suite and give it a name.
Click Add and choose the test cases you want to run. Then save the suite.

steps.t: Click Run and choose a browser
steps.d: Open the Run drop-down arrow, pick a browser, and run the suite.
steps.cap: Your Test Suite, the Run button and its browser list. This screenshot comes from an example project, so your test names will be different.

steps.d: Watch the Job Progress panel on the right. It shows the suite while it runs, then displays the final result, such as "3 Passed".

parts.s: Time to find out what happened during the run.

steps.d: After the run, open the Log Viewer at the bottom. At the top you will see how many tests passed, failed, had errors, were incomplete or were skipped. Click any step to read its status and any error message.
steps.cap: The Log Viewer after a Test Suite run. This screenshot comes from an example project, so your test names will be different.

parts.s: A report is a summary of the whole run that you can review or share.

steps.d: After running a Test Suite, open its Result tab. You can also open Reports in Tests Explorer and choose the latest run. You will see the status of each test case and a summary.
steps.cap: The report opened inside Katalon Studio. This screenshot comes from an example project, so your test names will be different.

steps.t: Find the report on your computer
steps.d: Open your project folder, then Reports, then the latest execution folder. If your project settings create an HTML report, open it in your browser.
steps.cap: The Reports folder in the project on your computer. The folder names are based on the date and time of the run.

steps.d:
In any report, check:
• the overall status
• which test cases passed or failed
• how long the run took
• the error details, if something failed
steps.note: The available report formats can differ by Katalon version and project settings.

concepts: A group of test cases that run together.
Starts your test or suite in the browser you pick.
Shows every step of a run and its status.
A panel that shows a run while it is happening.
A summary of the results of a whole run.
One complete run of a test or suite.
help: The browser does not open
Check that the browser is installed on your computer and that it works with your version of Katalon Studio.
The test cannot find an element
Check that the web page looks the way it did when you recorded, and check the Test Object saved in the Object Repository.
I cannot find the report
Open the latest execution folder inside Reports, and make sure the suite finished running.
check: I ran my test case using Chrome
I created or opened a Test Suite and ran it
I found the final result in the Log Viewer
I opened the latest report and found the result of my test
done: I can run one test case and a Test Suite
I can find a failed step and read its error
I can find the generated report without any help

TestOps: Connect Katalon Studio to TestO.sum: Connect Katalon Studio to TestOps so your local test results upload automatically.
TestOps: Connect Katalon Studio to TestO.intro: So far your tests ran only on your computer. TestOps is Katalon's online home for test results. In this lesson you will connect Katalon Studio to TestOps, so that each time you run a Test Suite, the report is sent there automatically. Your whole team can then see it.
obj: Connect a Katalon Studio project to Katalon TestOps
Turn on automatic test report uploads
Run a Test Suite on your computer
Confirm the result appears in TestOps
need: Katalon Studio installed, and you are signed in
Access to your team's Katalon TestOps organization and project
A training project with at least one working test case saved inside a Test Suite. Need one? See Lesson 3
An internet connection

info.d:
You still run your tests on your computer in Katalon Studio. After a Test Suite finishes, Katalon sends the report to the TestOps project you choose.
1Katalon StudioYour Test Suite runs on your computer
2Integration settingsYou pick your TestOps project
3Run the Test SuiteThe report uploads after the run
4Katalon TestOpsYou review the test results online

info.t: What will you see in TestOps?
info.d:
Passed The test finished successfully.
Failed A step or check did not pass.
Error A problem happened during the run.
No report Check that you ran a Test Suite, picked the right project and turned on uploads.
info.tip: Remember: running a single test case does not upload its report. Add the test case to a Test Suite and run the suite instead.

parts.s: You only need to do this once for each project.

steps.d: Start Katalon Studio, sign in, and open your training project.
Go to Project ▸ Settings, then choose Katalon TestOps Integration from the list.
steps.note: Depending on your Studio version, this may be called Katalon True Platform, or you may find it under Integration. Choose the one that matches.
steps.cap: Project ▸ Settings in the top menu. This screenshot comes from an example project, so your names will be different.

steps.d: Tick Enable Katalon TestOps Integration (or Enable Katalon True Platform Integration).
steps.cap: The settings page: tick the Enable box, choose your project and keep the upload box ticked. This screenshot comes from an example project, so your names will be different.

steps.d: Pick your team's project from the Project drop-down. Don't see it? Click Fetch Projects to refresh the list, and check that your account has access to it.
Tick Automatically upload all test reports to Katalon TestOps. In some versions it is named Automatically submit test run result.
Click Apply and Close. Your project is now ready to send reports to TestOps.

parts.s: Let's run a Test Suite and see the result appear online.

steps.d: In Tests Explorer, open Test Suites and select your training suite. Click Run and choose Chrome (or another browser you have installed).
Wait for the run to finish. Then look at the Job Progress panel and make sure the report was generated and uploaded. If you see View on Katalon TestOps or View result, you can click it.
steps.cap: Job Progress shows "Generated and uploaded test reports". Test Runs lists the run under Katalon True Platform. This screenshot comes from an example project, so your names will be different.

steps.d: Sign in to Katalon TestOps and open the same project you chose in Studio.
Open Executions ▸ History (the name may differ slightly). Find your latest run, then check the result, the status of each test case, the logs and how long it took.
steps.cap: The Executions History page in TestOps shows the uploaded run with its results. This screenshot comes from an example project, so your names will be different.

concepts: Katalon's online place to store and view test results.
The connection between Katalon Studio and TestOps.
A group of test cases that run together.
The panel that shows a run and its upload.
One run of a suite, as shown in TestOps.
The TestOps folder where your team's results are stored.
help: My project is missing
Make sure you are signed in with the right Katalon account and that you have access to the organization and project. Then click Fetch Projects again.
The upload failed
Check your internet connection and the integration settings. Read the upload message in Job Progress for the reason.
I can't see my report in TestOps
Check that you picked the right TestOps project, that the Test Suite finished, and that you ran a suite, not a single test case. Then refresh TestOps.
The menu names look different
Studio versions may say TestOps Integration, Katalon Platform or Katalon True Platform. Follow the integration settings that match your version.

I turned on automatic report uploads
I ran one Test Suite on my computer
I opened the uploaded result in TestOps
I can show my trainer the Test Suite name and its status

I can run a local Test Suite
I can find its uploaded report in Katalon TestOps

TestOps: Create Manual & Automated Test.sum: Write a manual test case in TestOps and see how your automated tests fit in.
TestOps: Create Manual & Automated Test.intro: TestOps is more than a place to see results. You can also write test cases there. In this lesson you will create a manual test case with steps and expected results. Then you will see how automated tests made in Katalon Studio are managed and reported in TestOps.
obj: Create a manual test case with steps and expected results in TestOps
Organize your test case in a folder
Understand how automated tests from Katalon Studio are managed in TestOps
Tell the difference between manual and automated test cases
need: You can sign in to your organization and project in Katalon TestOps
You have permission to create or edit test cases in the project
Katalon Studio is installed and connected to TestOps. Not yet? See Lesson 4

info.d:
Both ways end up in TestOps, but they start in different places.
Manual in TestOps1: Create the test case
2: Add steps and expected results
3: Save and organize it
Automation + TestOps1: Record or script it in Katalon Studio
2: Run the connected Test Suite
3: Review the results in TestOps

ManualCreated in: TestOps
Run by: a tester who follows the steps
Results: recorded in test management
Best for: exploring and human checks
AutomatedCreated in: Katalon Studio
Run by: Katalon, using scripted steps
Results: uploaded after a supported run
Best for: repeatable regression checks
info.tip: Important: TestOps manages test cases and results. The scripts that Katalon runs are written and kept in Studio. Creating a manual test case in TestOps does not turn it into an automation script.

steps: Open the OrangeHRM demo login URL
Enter the demo username and password
scn.note: Use the current demo credentials shown on the demo page. Never store real passwords in a test case description.

parts.t: Create a manual test case in TestOps
parts.s: You will write the steps a person would follow to test the login.

steps.d: Sign in to TestOps, then select your organization and project.
steps.cap: The Katalon login page. Sign in with the method your team uses.

steps.d: Check that your project is selected at the top left. Then open Tests ▸ Test Cases.
steps.note: Menu names may differ a little between TestOps versions.
steps.cap: Choosing your project from the drop-down at the top left. This screenshot comes from an example project, so your names will be different.

steps.d:
Click Create, then Create new test case. Use this title:
TC_MAN_001 – Verify OrangeHRM login
steps.cap: The Create menu in the Test Cases page. This screenshot comes from an example project, so your names will be different.

steps.d: Enter the steps and expected results from the example above, one step per row. Then save the test case.
steps.tip: Click Add new row for each step. You can also press Tab at the end of the last step to add the next one.
steps.cap: A manual test case with steps, expected results and test data. This screenshot comes from an example project, so your names will be different.

parts.t: Create an automated test and link it to TestOps
parts.s: Automated tests are made in Katalon Studio. TestOps then tracks them and their results.

steps.d: Open the project you connected to TestOps in Lesson 4.
Use Record Web (Lesson 2), or Manual / Script view, to automate the OrangeHRM login steps. Add a verification that the Dashboard is displayed.
Save it as TC_AUTO_001_Verify_OrangeHRM_Login and add it to a Test Suite.
Run the suite on your computer. Make sure the report upload to TestOps is turned on for your project.
Open your TestOps project and look at the uploaded execution results. Where your workspace supports it, synchronize or link the automated test to its test case record in TestOps.

concepts: A set of steps to check one thing.
Steps a person follows, written in TestOps.
A test that Katalon runs by itself, made in Studio.
What should happen after a step.
Values used in a step, like a web address.
A place to keep related test cases together.
help: I can't create test cases
Check that you have access to the project and the right role permissions. Ask your KT lead if you are not sure.
No automated result appears

My automated test is not listed as a test case

check: I created one manual login test case with at least three steps and expected results
I created or reused one automated login test in Katalon Studio
I ran the automated test in a Test Suite
I found the execution in TestOps and can explain its status

TestOps: Create Test Suites.sum: Group your manual and automated test cases into a Test Suite in TestOps.
TestOps: Create Test Suites.intro: A Test Suite is a group of related test cases, such as everything that checks the OrangeHRM login. In this lesson you will create a Test Suite in TestOps, add the test cases from Lesson 5, and review it. You will not run it yet.
obj: Create a Test Suite in TestOps
Add existing manual and automated test cases to it
Review the suite before it is run
need: You can sign in to Katalon TestOps and open your training project
You have test cases from Lesson 5 (manual, and/or automated ones that were synchronized). Need them? See Lesson 5
You have permission to create and manage Test Suites

info.d:
A Test Suite is a group of related test cases with one testing purpose. It helps you manage what is covered. You make one in four steps:
1OpenYour TestOps project
2CreateA new Test Suite
3AddExisting test cases
4ReviewSave and check it
info.tip: Creating a suite does not run the tests. It only groups them.

info.d: Manual cases are done by a tester in a manual test run. Automated cases need an automation setup, such as a connected Katalon Studio project. A suite only organizes cases. It does not turn manual steps into automation.

Here is the kind of suite you will build. Use your own Lesson 5 test cases.
TC_LOGIN_001 Verify login with valid credentials Manual
TC_LOGIN_002 Verify login with invalid credentials Manual
TC_LOGIN_003 Verify successful login Automated
info.tip: These IDs are only examples. An automated case must already be in TestOps before you can select it.

parts.s: Follow these six steps. Take your time and check each one.

steps.d: Open TestOps and select your training organization and project.
steps.cap: The Katalon login page.

steps.d: Go to the test management area and find Test Suites.
steps.note: Menu labels and layout may differ by TestOps version or workspace.

steps.d: Click Create ▸ Test Suite. Name it OrangeHRM_Login_Test_Suite. For the description, write: Verify the OrangeHRM login feature.
steps.cap: Create ▸ Test Suite on the Test Suites page. This screenshot comes from an example project, so your names will be different.

steps.d: Use the Add Test Case action. Search for the login test cases from Lesson 5, click the + beside each one you want, and confirm.
steps.note: Choose MANUAL as the suite type if you are creating a manual suite.
steps.cap: Choosing MANUAL, and the + buttons that add test cases. This screenshot comes from an example project, so your names will be different.

steps.d: Open the Test Case List and check that your selected test cases are there. Then save or confirm, as your workspace asks.
steps.cap: Two test cases chosen. Their count shows in Test Case List. This screenshot comes from an example project, so your names will be different.

steps.d: Open the Test Suite again. Check its name, its description and the test cases inside.
steps.warn: Do not start an execution in this lesson.

concepts: A group of related test cases.
A suite carried out by a tester during a manual test run.
A test Katalon runs, which must be available in TestOps first.

Custom Keywords in Katalon Studio.sum: Write a reusable keyword once, then use it in any test case.
Custom Keywords in Katalon Studio.intro: Imagine writing the same check in 20 different tests. Then the page changes, and you must fix all 20! A Custom Keyword solves this. You write the check once, give it a name, and call it wherever you need it. In this lesson you will build a keyword that checks the text of a heading, and use it in a real test.
obj: Understand why Custom Keywords are useful
Create a reusable text check using Groovy
Use the keyword in a local Web UI test case
Read Passed and Failed results in the Log Viewer
need: Katalon Studio installed, with your training Web project open
A saved test case, and a captured Test Object for a text element you can see. Need these? See Lesson 2
The practice site: https://katalon-demo-cura.herokuapp.com/. Its home page heading says CURA Healthcare Service.

info.d:
A Custom Keyword is a reusable piece of Groovy code. Instead of writing the same check in many test cases, you create it once and call it whenever you need it. Here is the plan for this lesson:
1CreateThe Keywords folder
2CodeA Groovy keyword
3CallIt in a test case
4RunIn a local browser
5CheckThe Log Viewer
info.tip: You will copy and paste the code, so you do not need to be a programmer. Just follow the steps carefully.

info.d:
Our keyword is named verifyTextEquals. It needs two things:
element The page element you saved earlier, like the heading.
expectedText The text you expect to see.
It reads the text that is shown on the page and compares it with your expected text. If they are different, the test fails.

parts.s: You will make a keyword package, a keyword class, and add the code.

steps.d: In Tests Explorer, right-click Keywords, then choose New ▸ Package. Type the name customKeywords and click OK. If you already have a package, you can use it.
steps.cap: Right-click Keywords, then New ▸ Package. This screenshot comes from an example project, so your folders will be different.

steps.d: Right-click the customKeywords package, then choose New ▸ Keyword. Name it TextAssertions and click OK. Katalon creates a Groovy class for you.
steps.cap: The New Keyword window. Your Package field will show customKeywords. This screenshot comes from an example project, so your folders will be different.
The finished keyword file, TextAssertions.groovy. This screenshot comes from an example project, so your folders will be different.

steps.d: Use Spy Web or Record Web to save the CURA home page heading in the Object Repository. Give it a clear name, such as Page_Home/heading_CURA.
steps.warn: Make sure the object points to the heading only, not the whole page.
steps.cap: Spy Web (Object Spy) with the CURA address, ready to capture the heading.

steps.d:
Open your test case and switch to Script view with the tab at the bottom. Use this sample:
import static com.kms.katalon.core.testobject.ObjectRepository.findTestObject
import com.kms.katalon.core.webui.keyword.WebUiBuiltInKeywords as WebUI

WebUI.openBrowser('')
WebUI.navigateToUrl('https://katalon-demo-cura.herokuapp.com/')
CustomKeywords.'customKeywords.TextAssertions.verifyTextEquals'(
    findTestObject('Page_Home/heading_CURA'),
    'CURA Healthcare Service'
)
WebUI.closeBrowser()
steps.note: The object path is an example. Use the exact folder and name from your Object Repository. The expected text must match the heading exactly.
steps.cap: The test case in Script view, calling the custom keyword.

Open the Log Viewer. If the heading matches, the keyword step passes. If it is different, the check fails and the test stops, because we chose STOP_ON_FAILURE.
steps.tip: Try it: change the expected text to Wrong Heading and run again. It should fail. Then read the failure message in the Log Viewer to see why.

Test Listeners in Katalon Studio.sum: Open and close the browser automatically, so you do not repeat it in every test.
Test Listeners in Katalon Studio.intro: Do you add "Open Browser" and "Close Browser" to every test case? That is a lot of repeating! A Test Listener does it for you. It is a small Groovy class that runs by itself before and after your test cases. In this lesson you will build one that opens the CURA website before a test and closes the browser after it.
obj: Explain what a Test Listener is and when it runs
Create a listener that opens and closes the browser
Write a test case without Open Browser or Close Browser steps
Run it locally and check the Log Viewer
need: Katalon Studio open with your local Web testing project
A saved Web test case that checks a page element but does not open or close the browser itself. Need one? See Lesson 2
The CURA demo website: https://katalon-demo-cura.herokuapp.com/

info.d:
A Test Listener is a Groovy class that runs actions when a certain test event happens. These events are called hooks:
@BeforeTestCase Runs before a test case starts.
@AfterTestCase Runs after a test case ends.
@BeforeTestSuite Runs before a test suite starts.
@AfterTestSuite Runs after a test suite ends.
info.tip: Think of a helper who opens the door before you walk in and closes it after you leave. You never have to ask.

info.d:
Your test case will only check the page. The listener will do the rest:
1Before testOpen the browser
2Test caseVerify the home page
3After testClose the browser

Careful A listener affects every test case in the project. Use this one only for the Web tests it is meant for.
No double work Do not open or close the same browser again inside the test case, or the actions can clash.
Mixed projects If you also have API or mobile tests, add conditions, or use a separate project.
Keep it clean Put your checks (assertions) in the test case, not in the listener.

Checkpoints in Katalon Studio.sum: Save expected database results and compare them with the live data.
Checkpoints in Katalon Studio.intro: Sometimes data in a database changes when it should not. A Checkpoint helps you catch that. It saves the expected result of a database query. When you run your test, Katalon runs the query again and compares the new result with the saved one. In this lesson you will create a Checkpoint for one employee record.

Create a Checkpoint and save the expected query result
Add a Verify Checkpoint step to a test case
Understand why a comparison passes or fails

A suitable JDBC driver, if your database needs one
A sample employees table, or a similar table from your trainer

info.d:
A database Checkpoint stores the expected results of a database query. When the test runs, Katalon compares the current query results with those saved values. This helps you spot unexpected data changes. Here is how it works:
1ConnectDatabase access
2QuerySelect test data
3SaveExpected values
4CompareActual vs expected
5ReviewPass or fail
info.tip: Use a record that does not change, so your Checkpoint stays steady.

scn.pre: Use training data only. Replace the example values with the real values from your own test database.
steps: Table: employees. Columns: employee_id, employee_name, status.
The row is 1001 · Maria Santos · Active.

Connecting Katalon Studio to GitHub.sum: Save your Katalon project on GitHub safely, using a feature branch.
Connecting Katalon Studio to GitHub.intro: Your automation tests are valuable, so keep them safe and share them with your team. Git and GitHub save every version of your project, so people can work together without overwriting each other. In this advanced lesson you will connect a Katalon project to GitHub, work on a feature branch, and safely commit, push and pull your changes.
obj: Connect a Katalon project to a GitHub repository
Create and use a feature branch
Stage, commit and push your changes safely
Pull the latest changes before new work
need: Katalon Studio installed, and a working automation project saved on your computer
Git installed. To check, open Terminal (Mac) or Command Prompt (Windows) and type git --version
A GitHub account with access to a repository, and permission to push to a feature branch
A personal access token (PAT) or an SSH key for signing in to GitHub. Do not use your GitHub password as a Git credential.
A backup of your project, or commit your current work, before you change any Git settings

info.d:
You work on your computer, save your work on a branch, then send it to GitHub for review:
1WorkKatalon Studio
2SaveLocal Git repository
3BranchFeature branch
4PushGitHub remote
info.tip: Local means the copy on your computer. Remote (called origin) is the copy on GitHub. A branch is your own safe space to work, so the main branch stays clean.

info.d:
git status See modified and untracked files.
git remote -v Check the connected GitHub remote.
git switch -c feature/katalon-training Create a feature branch and switch to it.
git add <file> Stage a specific file.
git commit -m "message" Save a version of your changes.
git push -u origin feature/katalon-training Upload your feature branch.
git fetch origin Get remote branch information.
git pull --ff-only Update your branch without creating a merge commit.
info.tip: The Git menu names in Katalon Studio change between versions. Terminal commands are the reliable way to do these steps.

parts.s: Check your tools and prepare the repository.

steps.d:
Open Terminal or Command Prompt and run this command. If Git is missing, install it from git-scm.com and restart Katalon Studio.
git --version
Open your project in Katalon Studio and look at the Git toolbar or menu. If the Git option is missing, turn on the Git integration plugin with the plugin option that your Katalon version offers.
On github.com, create a private repository for your training project, or use the one your team gave you. Copy its HTTPS or SSH clone URL.
steps.warn: If your project already has Git history, do not create unrelated starter commits in the new remote.

parts.s: Link your local project to the GitHub repository.

steps.d:
In Katalon Studio, use the Git sharing or initialization option if you can see it. Or open Terminal in your Katalon project folder and run:
git init
steps.note: Skip this step if your project already has a .git folder.

steps.d:
In Terminal, in your project folder, run this command. Replace the text in angle brackets with your own repository URL.
git remote add origin <repository-url>
steps.note: If origin already exists, check it with git remote -v. Do not add it twice.

steps.d: Create or check your .gitignore file before you stage anything. Leave out Reports/, test output, local caches, credentials, tokens and files that only belong to your computer.
steps.warn: Never commit real passwords in Profiles or test data.

parts.s: Make your changes safely, away from the main branch.

steps.d:
Run this command:
git switch -c feature/katalon-training
steps.note: If the branch already exists, switch to it instead. Avoid committing straight to a protected main branch.

steps.tip: Look at the staged changes before you commit.

steps.d:
Send your branch to GitHub. Sign in with your approved PAT or SSH setup when you are asked.
git push -u origin feature/katalon-training
Open your repository on GitHub in a browser. Switch to your feature branch and check that your test cases and project files are there. Create a Pull Request if your team needs a code review.

parts.s: Always update before you start new work.

steps.d:
Before you edit a shared branch, get the latest changes:
git fetch origin
git pull --ff-only

Run Tests Using Katalon Runtime Engine (.sum: Run a Test Suite from the command line and read its report, without clicking through Studio.
Run Tests Using Katalon Runtime Engine (.intro: So far you have pressed the Run button in Katalon Studio. But what if a test must run at night, on a server, or inside a CI/CD pipeline, where nobody is clicking buttons? That is the job of the Katalon Runtime Engine (KRE). It runs your Test Suite from a single command line. In this lesson you will generate that command, run it, and read the report.
obj: Explain what KRE is and when to use it
Generate a KRE command from Katalon Studio
Run the command in Terminal or Command Prompt
Find the report and tell if the run passed or failed
Fix the most common run errors
need: A Katalon Studio project with a saved Test Suite that already passes in Studio (for example, OrangeHRM_Login_Suite). Need a reminder? See Lesson 3
KRE installed or available through your company, with the right license and account access
A supported browser installed (for example Chrome), with compatible drivers
The path to your .prj file and the exact path of the Test Suite

info.d:
Katalon Runtime Engine (KRE) runs Katalon tests from a command line. It is made for runs without a screen and without clicking, such as:
Unattended runs Start a test and walk away.
Batch files Run several suites one after another.
CI/CD pipelines Let your build server run the tests for you.
A valid KRE license and activation may be required.
info.tip: Studio is your workshop where you build tests. KRE is the delivery truck that runs them anywhere.

scn.t: What should happen when you run it
scn.pre: Your Test Suite already passes in Katalon Studio, and you copied the KRE command.
steps: Paste it in Terminal or Command Prompt and press Enter.
KRE starts and prints logs and an execution status.
The browser may open and close by itself, then the terminal shows the final status.
Go to the Reports folder of your project.

scn.note: Run the suite in Studio first. If it fails there, it will also fail in KRE, and it is easier to fix in Studio.

parts.s: You will start from a working suite and let Studio build the command for you.

steps.d: Open Katalon Studio and run your Test Suite once. Confirm that it passes before you move to KRE.
Open the Test Suite and use the Generate Command option (the name and place can change between Studio versions). Choose the suite, the browser and the Execution Profile, then copy the command.
steps.note: The command from your own Studio version is the source of truth. Use the example below only to understand its parts.

steps.d:
Read the command and confirm these parts:
KRE program The location of katalonc (or katalonc.exe on Windows).
-projectPath The full path to your .prj file.
-testSuitePath The exact suite path, such as Test Suites/OrangeHRM_Login_Suite.
-browserType The browser, such as Chrome.
-executionProfile The profile, such as default.
Here is an example. Your paths will be different:
katalonc -noSplash -runMode=console -projectPath="/path/to/OrangeHRM.prj" -retry=0 -testSuitePath="Test Suites/OrangeHRM_Login_Suite" -browserType="Chrome" -executionProfile="default"
steps.warn: This is an example only. Replace the program and paths with your own values. Flags can change between Katalon versions.

parts.t: Run it and read the result
parts.s: Time to run your suite without opening Studio.

steps.d: On a Mac, open Terminal. On Windows, open Command Prompt or PowerShell. Go to the KRE folder, or use the full path to the program.
Paste the generated command and press Enter. Sign in or activate your license if asked.
steps.warn: Never put passwords or API keys in shared documents or in Git.

Open the Reports folder of your project and find the latest suite run. Open the HTML report, and look at the CSV and log files too. If something failed, find the failed test step.

ALM Integration: Jira and TestRail.sum: Connect Jira to Katalon True (TestOps) and TestRail to Katalon Studio, and know where each result goes.
ALM Integration: Jira and TestRail.intro: Real teams track requirements and bugs in tools like Jira, and test cases in tools like TestRail. These are called ALM tools. In this lesson you will learn two separate connections: Jira with Katalon True (TestOps), and TestRail Cloud with Katalon Studio. The most important idea is that these two connections are separate, so each one sends results to a different place.
obj: Connect Jira to Katalon True and synchronize requirements and defects
Set up TestRail Cloud in Katalon Studio and map a test case
Run a mapped suite and find the result
Explain which integration sends results where
need: A Katalon True account. You need Account Admin or System Admin for the account connection and Project Admin for the project settings
A Jira Cloud site, a Jira project and an Atlassian API token without scopes. The token owner needs Browse Projects, and Create Issues to create defects
Katalon Studio with an active license and the TestRail Integration plugin, plus a TestRail Cloud account with the API enabled
Existing test cases and a test suite to test the connection

info.d:
There are three paths. Only two are supported connections:
Jira → Katalon True / TestOps Account connection, project mapping, sync of requirements and defects, then traceability.
TestRail Cloud → Katalon Studio Install the plugin, connect, map case IDs, run suites and upload results.
TestRail ↔ Katalon True / TestOps Not a native connector in the current Katalon True catalog. Do not expect automatic sync.
info.tip: Think of two separate mailboxes. Jira results go to TestOps. TestRail results go to TestRail. One does not fill the other.

info.d:
1Jira work itemKatalon True requirements and defects
2Studio test suiteKatalon True execution report
3Studio test suite + pluginTestRail Cloud results

New screens The current Katalon True screens are different from the older TestOps Legacy guides. Follow the steps in this lesson.
Menus Exact menus can change with your permissions.
Secrets Never put API tokens in test scripts or in shared documents.
Self-hosted The official TestRail plugin documents TestRail Cloud, not self-hosted TestRail.

scn.pre: Use a Jira test project and training data only.
steps: Jira story QA-101: "User can sign in with valid credentials."
The story appears in Katalon True as a requirement.
Connect your login test case to that requirement.
You can trace the requirement to its test.
Run the test case from Katalon Studio.
The result shows in Katalon True.
Link or create a Jira defect.
Do not create a defect for a problem in the test itself.
scn.note: The goal is a clear line from the requirement to the test to the result.

parts.t: Part A: Connect Jira to Katalon True
parts.s: First at the account level, then at the project level.

steps.d: Sign in to Katalon True. Go to Account ▸ Integrations ▸ + Create Integration and choose Jira.

For Jira Cloud, enter an integration name, your Jira URL (like https://yourcompany.atlassian.net), the token owner email and the Atlassian API token without scopes. For Jira Data Center, use its HTTPS URL and a Data Center personal access token (PAT).
Click Test Connection, then Save. Check that the integration shows Active in Admin ▸ System ▸ Integrations.
steps.warn: If it shows Error, check the URL, the token and the permissions.

steps.d: Open your Katalon True project, then Settings ▸ Integrations. Open the settings (gear icon) of the linked Jira connection. Choose the Jira project and, if you want, a board.
Turn on Pull Requirements for requirements, releases and sprints, and/or Bug Mapping for defects. Review the priority, status, work item types and required fields, then click Proceed.
Open the requirements and look for your Jira work items. Use one sample test case and one defect to confirm the trace.

parts.t: Part B: Connect TestRail Cloud to Katalon Studio
parts.s: Here the connection lives inside Katalon Studio.

steps.d: In TestRail Cloud open Administration ▸ Site Settings ▸ API, enable the API and save. Ask your TestRail administrator if you cannot see it.
Install the official TestRail Integration plugin that matches your Studio version. Restart Studio if it asks.
In Studio go to Project ▸ Settings ▸ Plugins ▸ TestRail. Tick Enable TestRail. Enter your TestRail Cloud URL, username, the credential your plugin supports and the numeric TestRail project ID.
Click Test Connection. When it works, click Apply and Close.

In TestRail, find the case ID (example: C25). In Studio open the matching test case, go to the Integration tab and type the number only (25), then save. Some Studio versions allow several IDs separated by commas or semicolons.
Run the mapped test case inside a Test Suite. Check the result in the TestRail test run you chose.
steps.note: No result? Check the project ID, the mapping and any required TestRail fields.

concepts: Application Lifecycle Management. Tools that track requirements, tests and bugs.
A tool for work items such as stories and bugs.
A tool for managing test cases and test runs.
The Katalon platform, formerly called TestOps.
What the software must do, such as a Jira story.
A clear link from requirement to test to result.
A secret key that lets one tool talk to another.
Linking a Studio test case to a TestRail case number.
help: Jira Test Connection fails
Check the Jira Cloud URL, the unscoped token with the matching email, and the permissions.
Jira issues are not visible
Check the Jira project, the Pull Requirements option, the work item and status mapping, and run the sync again.
TestRail connection fails
Check the Cloud URL, that the API is enabled, the plugin version, the credential and the numeric project ID.
TestRail results do not show
Check the case ID mapping, that you ran a test suite, the result upload settings and any required custom fields.
TestOps has results but TestRail does not
These are two separate integrations. Check the TestRail plugin settings.

I can explain Jira to TestOps versus TestRail to Studio

Android Mobile Testing in Katalon Studio.sum: Set up an Android Emulator, record a mobile test with Appium, add a check, run it and read the results.
Android Mobile Testing in Katalon Studio.intro: Can you test an app on a phone without holding a phone? Yes! A Android Emulator lets you run a real mobile app on your computer, and Katalon Studio taps through it for you using a tool called Appium. In this lesson you will set up the Android Emulator, record a mobile test, add a check, run it and read the results. The setup takes the longest, so be patient.

Connect it to Katalon Studio through Appium
Record a mobile test and add a check
Run the test and read the results

Check that the expected screen or field is visible.

Open Terminal or Command Prompt and type:
node --version
npm --version
steps.note: You need Node.js 20.19 or newer and npm 10 or newer.

steps.d:
Run this command:
npm i --location=global appium@3.0.0

Run:
appium --version
appium driver list --installed

Run this command:
appium driver install uiautomator2@7.0.0
Then run appium driver list --installed again and confirm that your driver is listed.

parts.s: Get your phone ready before you open Katalon.

steps.d: Open Android Studio ▸ Device Manager ▸ Create Device. Pick a phone and install a matching Android system image.
Start the emulator and wait until the Android home screen shows.

Turn on Developer options and USB debugging, connect the phone with a USB cable and accept the trust prompt on the phone.

steps.d:
You can install the sample app by hand:

steps.note: Replace the path with the real location of APIDemos.apk.

parts.s: Tell Katalon where Appium lives.

steps.d: Open Katalon Studio ▸ Preferences (or Settings) ▸ Katalon ▸ Mobile.
Choose the real Appium folder. Run npm root -g to find your global npm folder. The Appium folder is usually inside it.
Go to File ▸ New ▸ Project ▸ Mobile. Choose the official sample project if you can, or Blank and add your app file.
Open the Run dropdown and confirm that your device is listed.

parts.s: You will let Katalon watch your taps and write the steps.

steps.d: Click Record Mobile (or Smart Mobile Recorder). Choose Local Device and select your Android Emulator.
Choose Application File and browse to APIDemos.apk. Click Start.
Wait until the app opens and its objects show in Device View. Use Interactive Mode if you see it.
Tap and type in Device View, and check that every action shows in Recorded Actions.
Add a check that an element exists or shows the right text. Use a stable captured object.
steps.warn: Do not only check that a tap happened. That does not prove the app works.

steps.d: Replay the steps while the recorder is open. Fix any missed action, then save the test case and the captured objects.

parts.t: Strengthen the check in Script view
parts.s: A short script makes your check clear.

steps.d:
Open the Script tab and add this after the navigation step:
import static com.kms.katalon.core.testobject.ObjectRepository.findTestObject
import com.kms.katalon.core.mobile.keyword.MobileBuiltInKeywords as Mobile

Mobile.verifyElementExist(findTestObject('Object Repository/Mobile/expectedElement'), 10)
steps.warn: expectedElement is a placeholder. Replace it with an object you captured with Mobile Recorder.
steps.note: For a stronger check, use verifyElementText or another mobile check against the real expected result.

parts.s: See the test run on the Android Emulator.

steps.d: Save it. In the Run dropdown choose Android or iOS and pick your device. Click Run and watch Katalon open the app and tap through the steps.
Check Passed or Failed and find the first failing step. Look at the Console for Appium and driver errors.

steps.t: Run it as a Test Suite
steps.d: Add the test case to a Test Suite and run the suite. Open the latest Reports folder to see the HTML report.
steps.note: If TestOps integration is on, reports upload automatically for Test Suites and Test Suite Collections, not for a single test case run.

A virtual phone that runs on your computer.

Make sure the emulator or simulator is fully started. Check adb devices.
The app does not launch
Check the app type, the phone version, the file type, whether the app is installed, and the device family.
Appium or driver error
Check Appium 3, the driver version, the Appium Directory and that your Katalon version fits.
Element not found
Spy the element again, check its locator, wait for the screen to load, and handle any permission pop-ups.

The app installs and opens without errors
Mobile Recorder captured my planned actions
My test has at least one meaningful check

I ran a Test Suite and found its report

I can record, check and run a mobile test
